newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat-Light hail damage reported.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat-Light hail damage reported.

text.p: A severe storm pounded parts of southern Minnesota and eastern North Dakota early Thursday, causing light hail damage to some wheat fields, cash grain dealers said.
"They got blasted with a lot of severe weather, a lot of hail and torrential rain," said Dave Taylor, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.
Cash sources said farmers were still scouting fields but several reported broken stalks.
Spring wheat bids were mostly higher but farmer selling remained at a virtual standstill.
The worst weather missed Montana where hard red winter wheat harvest continued.

"We've got a couple of farmers who say they're going to start harvesting tomorrow," a northern Montana dealer said. "I think we're going to have low protein but it looks like yield-wise, we're going to have a fantastic crop."
Several dealers said expectations of a large winter wheat crop would cut spring wheat bids in the next few days.
"The premiums are breaking," a Minnesota dealer said. "People's needs have been filled. We're getting some new crop winter wheat out here already."
